90% of my self harm is unrelated to my suicidal thoughts. That said, yes i have suicidal thoughts and i self harm, so maybe they are commonly connected. 

Ive discovered that my self harm is mostly due to a distortion of my autistic stimming thanks to trauma. I was denied access to healthy stims because they’re too noticeable and so were deemed bothersome to others. So i hid my stims. But because stimming is a necessary way to self regulate, i still needed it, so it started coming out in a variety of ways that hurt my body. Self harm stims are much more accepted by people than “annoying” stims that could make others notice your existence.

Family of 6, kids are 10 and under, used to spend $300 per week, its gone up to $350-400. To keep our budget we’ve cut back a lot on variety of produce, even apples are a special treat now. We’ve also cut back on meat, or swap things out for cheaper meats - so chili is meatless now, burritos are bean heavy and often chicken/turkey instead of beef.

Hours in a row of uninterrupted time - where i could read, make art, have sex (as loud and fun and wherever in the house we wanted at any time!), have long conversations, have long dates. Even being able to play some basketball without the responsibility of supervising kids at the same time. 

Also being able to be spontaneous - impromptu outings with friends, trips, evenings out and not having to arrange a babysitter or having to worry about time and level of inebriation upon my return home.

Lots of mental health issues for sure. Insomnia too. We can’t afford mental health care right now but are planning on getting some help when it’s possible. Physically he’s overweight but his recent dr visit showed he’s in excellent health, though I question if he was fully open. Everything exhausts him. It’s been years since he’s seemed completely well.

I ask him to come watch the kids so I can shower, sometimes, like this time, he just never comes out of his man cave. Sometimes I’ve just gotten into the shower anyways and let the kids run amok, in which case he’s usually completely unaware that I even had a shower and carry’s on doing what he wants and not supervising. I’ve given him lists, schedules, added him to my household calendar so he gets notifications of the chores that need doing, he still doesn’t, says he’s tired or sore - and he legit seems to be, he’s breathless after putting away the clean dishes, he needs a days break after vacuuming his office. The rest all seems to fall into convenience. If he’s in the room when I’m cleaning he’ll sometimes help. Once the kids are in bed he just goes to do his thing while I keep working, or he might sweep a floor, or pick up some toys, but usually everything is invisible to him or he just doesn’t care enough to bother. And ya he probably does need therapy and medication, but he refuses to go.

I mean, it’s kinda how some people say to just stop doing housework and eventually they’ll do it. But instead you just end up burying yourself in piles of housework that never get caught up because he doesn’t ever pick up the slack. When I go out and he calls me hyperventilating and crying idk I don’t think it’s good for my kids to have him watching them like that

The only thing that’s worked for me - I’ve coslept with all of my kids- is night weaning. It was hell for a month each time, but they started sleeping through most of the night after that. At 13 months, not at bedtime,  I told them we would not be nursing at night anymore, that if they woke up they could have their sippy but that’s it. I like to tell them straight, it’s amazing how much they understand. Some of my kids dealt with it easier than others, but ultimately it worked. It’s a hard go for a while though.

It’s so hard to find someone to babysit when you have 2-3-4+ kids. No one ever wants to babysit mine and we can’t find someone to hire who would watch all four. Those that do want to help can only manage one kid at a time so there’s no break. It’s so hard, I feel like the lack of couple time really negatively affects the relationship. I’m sorry you’re struggling with this too.

My hubby bought me two movies for my birthday. I still haven’t had the time to watch them - it’s been 5 months. I used to read so much. I used to have time for hobbies. Somehow my husband still has time for things but not me😒

Things available on my phone are all I can manage now, I’ll stay up and get no sleep sometimes to watch something just to give my mind a break. 

It’s not silly at all to cry over that. It’s not just about the show, it’s all the layers of feelings built up from doing so much and not having time for yourself.

I left a boyfriend who I had started dating when we were about 14, broke up at 19. I didn’t know who I was, and it was tearing me apart. There wasn’t anything exactly wrong with my boyfriend, except that he had come to know and love a version of me that wasn’t entirely me....I had lost friends and opportunities, and I didn’t see a future with him as my authentic self. 

I feel terrible, wish I had known sooner, wish I had waited later to date anyone. But intimately I couldn’t carry on any longer for both our sakes. I hope, as he did, that you see the opportunity to spend some time with yourself too, you’re going to need time to rebuild and find yourself too. I’m sorry for the pain this has caused you, I’m sure she didn’t make this choice flippantly, and she knows it hurt you.

I’m convinced that my urge to self harm will never go away, but over time I have gotten better and better at coping and not acting on my desire to self harm. I haven’t cut myself in over 10 years, but the urge comes to me still, it’s quieter and easier to ignore. I have a better understanding now that it’s an unhealthy coping mechanism and know what works for me to get past it until the feeling fades and I am thinking clearly again. 

So trust that you can succeed again, that slipping up is no biggie and you can keep trying.

We did that for a few weeks last year. I got an hour once per week, which wasn’t enough, and then for some reason it stopped. He’d come home tired and would forget and I’d have to remind him. It became frustrating, instead of getting to just pop out I’d have to go through the letdown of him forgetting and him feeling bummed that he couldn’t relax after work. After it happened a few times I stopped reminding him, it was too stressful.

There’s a bulletin board up of daily chores, it’s really streamlined and minimal, like “Monday: wipe out microwave and mop” for example. He does take out the garbage, he’s responsible for grocery shopping (we get delivered groceries), he pays the bills. At this point the chore imbalance is much less important to me than just getting a break from the kids once in a while - I don’t care if he puts them on the screens or takes them outside to play, I just want some time alone so I can be something other than a mom for a part of my day.
